subject: Follow-up: model fit evals & tool-calling JSON compliance
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@astrahealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0000
Subject: Follow-up: model fit evals & tool-calling JSON compliance

Hi Alex

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps to validate model fit for the clinical summarization + payer-lookup flow you demoed: 

What we heard:
- Primary goal: extract structured reimbursement codes and produce a JSON summary for downstream billing systems.
- SLAs: <200ms P50 generation for short summaries; tolerate up to 1s for complex cases.
- Success metric: JSON schema compliance (no missing required fields) + <1% regression on the key-value extraction benchmark.

Recommended short list of model variants to evaluate (hosted):
- redwood-encoder-xxl-v2 (recommended for accuracy)
- redwood-latency-optimized-1 (recommended to test latency-sensitive paths)
- redwood-quant-4x (for cost/perf tradeoffs)

What we attached and shared:
- prompt_set_v1.csv  initial labeled prompts and expected JSON outputs for your sample cases (attached).
- eval_report_v1.pdf  preliminary run on a 200-case subset we discussed (attached).
- Benchmark link: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/astrhealth/structured-output-2026 (public/read-only for this thread).

Open technical questions for your team to confirm before we run the full eval:
1) Can you confirm the exact JSON schema (field names + types) you require? We used the one from your demo but want the canonical spec.
2) How should we handle retries and partial failures? E.g., should the API attempt a single auto-retry on transient failures, or should the client handle backoff?
3) Any PII handling constraints we should enforce on the eval cluster (redaction rules, allowed tokens, retention)?

Proposed next steps:
- You: share canonical JSON schema and one representative EHR export (sanitized).
- We: run structured-output eval across the three model variants above, produce per-field precision/recall, JSON schema compliance rate, and a performance/cost matrix. Estimated turnaround: 3 business days once we have schema + sample.
- Quick sync: 30 min next Wed to review results and pick model + quantization profile.

Looping in Dylan (SE) and Dev (platform) to weigh in on the JSON validation options and retry semantics.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.csv, eval_report_v1.pdf

From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@astrahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@astrahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 12:18:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit evals & tool-calling JSON compliance

Hi Marissa

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) JSON schema: we'll provide our canonical schema (includes patient_id, encounter_id, codes: [{code_type, code_value, confidence}], reimbursement_estimate, flags). I'll share the proto/schema by EOD. Important: the downstream system treats code_value as REQUIRED, code_type optional.

2) Retries: we'd prefer the service to perform an internal single retry on HTTP 5xx or network timeouts, then surface a structured error if still failing. If a partial result is returned (e.g., missing required code_value), we want the option to invalidate the response rather than accept partials. Can Redwood support a strict mode for schema enforcement?

3) PII: we will sanitize patient identifiers but won't risk sending PHI. Redaction rules are internal; we will send a sanitized sample tomorrow.

Can Dylan or Dev speak to the strict schema enforcement and how the SDK reports validation errors? Also cost sensitivity: if quantized model options produce small regressions, can we view a per-field delta so we can trade accuracy vs cost?

Thanks,
Alex

Alex Nguyen
Lead Product Manager, Integration Platform | AstraHealth
alex.nguyen@astrahealth.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@astrahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:40:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit evals & tool-calling JSON compliance

Thanks Alex quick technical notes: 

Strict schema enforcement: yes, we can run evals in two modes:
- permissive: model output is post-processed with a best-effort JSON parser and missing optional fields are backfilled when possible;
- strict: we validate against your canonical JSON schema and mark any non-compliant outputs as failures.

Retries: the Redwood SDK/server supports a one-attempt auto-retry for transient 5xx/timeouts by default; we can enable-trace logging for retries so you can audit when they happen. For strict mode, we do NOT auto-accept partial outputs the evaluation harness will mark them as schema failures.

Tool/function-calling notes: for your payer-lookup step we recommend implementing function-calls with the following pattern:
- Provide a resilient function contract (name + input schema) that the model must return.
- If the model returns invalid JSON, fall back to a deterministic extractor (our KV cache + regex tier) and flag the result.

Per-field delta reporting: our eval report includes per-field precision/recall/F1 and delta against a baseline model; the attached eval_report_v1.pdf has an example page showing the per-field deltas across redwood-encoder-xxl-v2 vs redwood-quant-4x. We'll output a CSV with the per-case diffs as well if that helps.

Security/PII: note that hosted evals in our restricted tenant will not persist tokens beyond 72h and we can enable additional KMS-based encryption for your samples in the dedicated eval run. We'll coordinate with security once you confirm.

Next actions from our side:
- Marissa: once we get the canonical schema and sanitized sample, I'll kick off the run.
- Alex/Sarah: please attach the schema + one sanitized EHR export (CSV or JSON).

Happy to hop on a quick technical call if you want to walk through the strict mode and function-calling flow.

Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
